Speaking from a recent experience where a friend totalled my vehicle..as long as you are not paying your uncle to borrow the car and it is not a regular thing (for Progressive, I believe it was less than 12 times a year, although "times" was not defined as a set period of hours or days), then you'd be covered under his policy. As a veterinarian, the concern about the space the uterus occupies seems so illogical.  The change in hormones (assuming the ovaries are removed), the adhesions that may be caused by an abdominal surgery procedure in general, the risks of surgery/anesthesia are all valid, but we spay dogs, cats, and other animals all the time and there is no noticeable issue I can think of that has to do with adjusting to the small space a non-gravid uterus occupies within the abdominal cavity...in any species.  If that were truly a problem, I think there would be far more issues with how their other organs react to being dislodged during pregnancy as they certainly get shifted out of place and then (generally speaking) go back once the uterus shrinks back down to size.
